column1: The Federal Reserve's Response to the Global Financial Crisis and Its Long-Term Impact: An Interrupted Time-Series Natural Experimental Analysis

The thesis titled The Federal Reserve's Response to the Global Financial Crisis and Its Long-Term Impact: An Interrupted Time-Series Natural Experimental Analysis by Arnaud Cedric Kamkoum  dated May 20  2023  investigates the monetary policies implemented by the Federal Reserve in response to the Global Financial Crisis. The study focuses on the Federal Reserve's quantitative easing (QE) programs  liquidity facilities  and forward guidance operations conducted from 2007 to 2018. The research employs an interrupted time-series (ITS) analysis to assess the long-term causal effects of the QE programs on U.S. inflation and real GDP.

The findings from this design-based natural experimental approach indicate that the QE operations had a positive impact on U.S. real GDP but did not significantly affect U.S. inflation. Specifically  during the post-QE period from the second quarter of 2011 to the fourth quarter of 2018  U.S. real GDP per capita increased by an average of 231 dollars per quarter compared to a scenario without the QE programs. Furthermore  by the fourth quarter of 2018  ten years after the initiation of the QE programs  real GDP per capita in the U.S. was 14% higher than it would have been without these programs. These results challenge Williamson's (2017) informal natural experimental evidence and align with the conclusions of vector autoregressions (VARs) and new Keynesian dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models  which suggest that the Federal Reserve's QE policies positively influenced U.S. real GDP.

The study also posits that the current high inflation rates in the U.S. and globally are likely not a result of the QE programs implemented in response to the financial crisis associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. Instead  they are probably due to the unprecedentedly large fiscal stimulus packages  the unique nature of the financial downturn itself  negative supply shocks from the war in Ukraine  or a combination of these factors. To the author's knowledge  this paper is the first to measure the macroeconomic effects of QE using a design-based natural experimental approach.

The paper contributes to the literature in three significant ways. First  it offers a clear and practical classification of domestic balance sheet policies by categorizing expansionary and contractionary policies into mutually exclusive categories: quantitative easing (QE) and quasi-quantitative easing (qQE)
column2: and quantitative tightening (QT) and quasi-quantitative tightening (qQT). This classification helps overcome the confusion caused by overlapping categories in existing studies. Second  it provides a comprehensive introduction to the natural experimental method of interrupted time-series (ITS) analysis  which is a special type of time series used to estimate the impact of an intervention. Although ITS analysis is widely used in evaluating healthcare and education policies  its application in estimating the effects of monetary policy on inflation and real output is limited. The overview of the ITS analysis method presented in this essay aims to increase its use in macroeconomics. Third  the paper is one of the few studies to examine the macroeconomic effects of monetary policy using a formal design-based natural experimental approach  and it is the first to use this method to measure the macroeconomic effects of QE.

column1: The thesis was part of the author's master's thesis written at Bursa Uludag University and is freely accessible online. The author  Arnaud Cedric Kamkoum  holds a Master of Arts in economics  a Bachelor of Science in mathematics  and a Bachelor of Arts in economics  all with high honors. He is a two-time recipient of the Hewlett Foundation MITx DEDP MicroMasters Scholarships and a two-time holder of the Turkish Government Scholarships.
